We closed a $5.5M pre-seed co-led by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, with Yellow, Evantic and Entrepreneur First, alongside angels from the founding teams of Spacemaker, Black Forest Labs, Hugging Face, Supabase, Cleo and Spore Bio. We already work with leading developers and expect to support hundreds of projects over the coming year, deepening our research, our hiring, and our coverage of the development process end to end.

Where We Operate

Early-stage development starts with a chain of high-stakes decisions, each requiring different data, different expertise, and different deliverables. Today, we deliver AI-powered outputs across the full spectrum - site sourcing, feasibility studies, architectural design, investment analysis, financial modeling, dataroom analysis, and more.

The Role

You will work on one of the core systems behind what Davis delivers. Our agents take raw, fragmented data and turn it into deliverables that real estate professionals use to make high-stakes decisions. Your job is to make that pipeline reliable, fast, and indistinguishable from work done by the best human teams - then push it beyond what any human team could do.

You can expect to:

  • Build and operate multi-agent systems that turn heterogeneous data into expert-grade deliverables across real estate development workflows.

  • Own the system end to end: infra, orchestration, context engineering, how the system selects, structures, and injects the right information so agents behave reliably at scale.

  • Ensure production-grade quality, performance, and reliability across every output we deliver to clients.

  • Sit with clients and domain experts regularly to understand their constraints, challenge your own assumptions, and make sure every output meets and even exceeds clients' expectations.

Beyond the technical depth, this role will expose you to how real estate decisions are made, how clients think, and what it takes to deliver outputs they trust. You'll develop a sharp business intuition alongside your engineering skills.

Key Responsibilities

  • Harness engineering: design and build the system layer around the model - context assembly, tool orchestration, verification, and report generation - to deliver consistent, high-quality outputs at scale.

  • Data ingestion & context assembly: handle messy, unstructured project data from heterogeneous sources and ensure agents have the right context at all times.

  • Storage & traceability: persist sources, extracted facts, intermediate results, report versions, and expert edits.

  • Expert-in-the-loop UX: design and build the review experience (annotations, edits, approvals, diffs/version history, provenance display).

  • Evaluation & benchmarking: build an internal eval harness (datasets, rubrics, regression tests, monitoring) to track agents performance over time.

What We're Looking For

  • 1.5+ years building and deploying production software at scale (APIs, reliability, testing, performance).

  • Experience building and evaluating LLM agents / multi-step workflows in real systems.

  • Proven context engineering experience: you've built systems where reliability depends on assembling the right context (RAG over heterogeneous sources, summarization, conversation state, tool outputs).

  • Deep Python expertise (clean architecture, typing, async/concurrency, strong testing culture).

  • Strong experience with databases + data modeling (structured storage, document storage, versioning).

  • Full-stack experience (you can ship a real UI), with a clear backend emphasis.

  • Comfortable building from first principles: we don't want heavy agent frameworks — we prefer a lightweight, well-engineered codebase.

Nice to Have

  • Experience operating LLM systems with observability and quality monitoring in production.

  • GIS familiarity (parcels, zoning layers, geocoding).

  • Multi-country product experience (heterogeneous sources, localization, varying rules).

  • NLP background

Why Join Us

You're joining a team of 9 at the very beginning - where every decision you make shapes the product, the culture, and the trajectory of the company. What you build here will be yours.

  • Direct impact on growth: your work doesn't sit behind three layers of review. You ship, clients use it, and you see the results. Every output you improve translates directly into revenue and reputation.

  • Real-world impact: your work supports investment decisions, accelerates development timelines, and helps redefine how cities are imagined, designed, and built.

  • High ownership: own the full feasibility stack end to end, as the CEO of that part.

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity in an early-stage company.

  • A small team with high standards - we ship fast and love working together.

More information about Davis, the team and the market we’re going after:

Team

Mehdi (Co-founder & CEO) grew up in a family of architects and has lived this problem firsthand. He's a repeat founder who bootstrapped his first startup at 20, and graduated from Sciences Po and HEC Paris. Amine (Co-founder & CTO) is an AI researcher from École Polytechnique who worked extensively on discrete diffusion and turned down a PhD with Google DeepMind to build Davis. They started working together in July 2025 at Entrepreneur First's first European residency, a two-month lock-in in a German castle.

Today we're a team of 12: technical profiles from Polytechnique, ENS and INRIA alongside architects and deep real estate expertise.

We're small with an extremely high bar. If you want to work deeply on hard problems and see your work reach clients within days, you're the one we need.

Why We'll Win

Real estate is a $13 trillion industry that technology has largely bypassed. The professional services that feed it (design, engineering, feasibility, permitting) represent hundreds of billions in spend that no one has seriously automated.

Proptech spent the last decade selling SaaS on the edges of these workflows. It didn't work, for two reasons: no professional wants another tool to learn, and no tool can automate work that runs on expert judgment. Davis makes a different bet. We don't sell tools, we sell the work: AI-generated, expert-validated, delivered in days instead of weeks. Every project compounds our data advantage across typologies, geographies and regulatory contexts.

Why No One Has Solved Architectural Design Yet

Real estate development bleeds time and money in architectural design loops. Architects cycle through dozens of floorplan revisions to meet regulatory and client constraints, each round taking days, each missed constraint restarting the loop. Traditional CAD and BIM tools offer zero generative capability; parametric tools only check constraints after generation, leading to designs that frequently break under new zoning rules or irregular sites.

Generative AI has the potential to solve this, but doesn't yet. Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

Fine-tuning image diffusion models on floorplans produces layouts that look plausible but fall apart under scrutiny: hallucinated rooms, mislabeled spaces, code violations no architect would accept. Pixel-space models have no concept of what a wall is or why a corridor needs to connect two things. Compliance-guidance techniques typically require segmentation at each noisy timestep, compounding errors and making major edits impractical. As a result, floorplans may “look” plausible but break building codes, or need heavy post-processing before they're usable.

Missions

 

🏗️ Alassio, en quelques mots

Le marché de la paie en cabinet d'expertise comptable est dominé depuis des décennies par des solutions historiques. Chez Alassio, notre ambition est de rénover le métier au bénéfice des gestionnaires de paie, avec un logiciel moderne, évolutif et pensé pour les réalités du terrain.

Lancé en juillet 2025 et déployé en clientèle depuis mars 2026, Alassio a levé 2,6 M€ en pre-seed auprès de Partech et de business angels de référence. Nous étendons en continu la couverture d'Alassio à de nouvelles conventions collectives et à de nouveaux dispositifs réglementaires. title: Change and Transformation Manager - Client Delivery (Fluency in French & English required)
description:
Change and Transformation Manager – Client Delivery (French/english)

Location: Paris, France (hybrid, three days a week in the office; occasional travel to Brussels and London)
Level: Programme Manager senior
Team: Client Delivery
Contract: Permanent
Reporting To: Operating Model Design Lead

Please note: This role is based in France, so you need to live here or be open to relocating, and it requires an existing right to work in the EU. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.

Fluent French and English (spoken and written) are essential, and we kindly ask you to submit your CV in English.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.

What you’ll do

  • Own change and transformation support for go-live readiness for ENGIE France’s migration onto Kaluza as the hands-on lead, from planning through cutover, hypercare and transition towards scaling, so ENGIE’s teams are ready and confident to adopt the platform from day one.

  • Decide the change approach for the programme: stakeholder analysis, change impact assessment, training design and business readiness engagement, shaped to ENGIE France’s operating context and owned by their teams.

  • Operate Kaluza’s business readiness governance: stage gates, readiness evidence, risk and dependency tracking and weekly reporting.

  • Partner with the Learning and Adoption Specialist in France to coordinate training, Train the Trainer and knowledge content, so enablement lands throughout each programme increment as we build out and release features via Agile delivery.

  • Be the day-to-day point of contact for ENGIE France on business readiness, change and adoption, giving practical change advice to their transformation leads.

  • Track adoption and operational stability through hypercare, root-cause any shortfall against acceptance criteria, and agree interventions with ENGIE.

  • Improve Kaluza’s readiness playbook: evolve what worked on ENGIE Belgium, test fixes where it falls short in France, and share what you learn with colleagues across Client Delivery to shape the platform’s operational foundations and improvements and to set our global standards.

Day to day, the activities you’ll lead or support include:

  • Change impact and readiness planning: diagnosing the full scope of impacts across roles, workflows, systems and customer experience, then turning them into a prioritised readiness plan sequenced against delivery, migration and release cadence.

  • Stakeholders, sponsors and change networks: mapping stakeholders and influence at workstream level, helping sponsors stay visible and engaged, and shaping the champion, superuser and people-manager networks that carry change into ENGIE’s business.

  • Communications and resistance: supporting ENGIE France’s own communications and engagement strategy, so their teams and customers hear a consistent, positive story about the programme. You’ll help leaders and champions advocate for the change, internally and with customers, and anticipate where resistance may form so you can intervene before it becomes entrenched.

  • Migration and go-live readiness: building the business and operational readiness evidence that enables a smooth transfer to service, measured against the agreed acceptance criteria, and supporting the go-live command centre.

  • Hypercare and stabilisation: agreeing hypercare entry and exit criteria, monitoring stability and adoption signals, and handing over cleanly to ENGIE’s business-as-usual teams.

  • Early releases and workarounds: planning for known limitations in early releases, and reflecting them in training, knowledge and communications so users are never caught by surprise. You’ll work with Release Management so each platform release arrives with the enablement it needs.

What you’ll bring

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Several years of hands-on change delivery on large platform or systems transformations, with a recognised change management discipline. You solve a wide range of problems creatively and work with little supervision.

  • Experience in regulated, customer-facing operational environments, including live customer account migration, cutover and go-live, where you have shaped the approach rather than only followed one.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management, credible with client programme leads and transformation sponsors.

  • Fluency in French and English, written and spoken.

  • Comfort working with data: you explore adoption and programme data yourself, report on it clearly and challenge decisions when evidence is weak.

  • Commercial awareness: you understand how Kaluza makes money and balance what the client needs against cost, working alongside SI partners and the client’s own change resources without duplicating effort.

What will set you apart: a background in energy retail or utilities, vendor-side experience on a SaaS implementation, and/or knowledge of contact centre operations and technology.

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

Our Perks

  • Financial & Insurance: Discretionary bonus, Alan Mutuelle Health Insurance, x3 Life & Death insurance (Prévoyance) via Alan, and standard Sécurité Sociale contributions (pension, family allowance, unemployment insurance)

  • Allowances: 50% commuting expense reimbursement, €200 Home Working Allowance, and €150 Learning Fund

  • Time Off & Flexibility: 25 days holiday + bank holidays + RTT days, Moments That Matter Leave, Compassionate Leave, two paid Volunteering Days, Flexible Working, and Career Break eligibility

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

Compensation: €56 – €75

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des entreprises innovantes comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Piloter la roadmap : porter la stratégie de bout en bout de Kaluza Agent Experience (KAE) sur le marché européen, en cohérence avec les objectifs produit globaux et affinée par les besoins clients locaux et les comportements des agents. Vous suivrez les indicateurs opérationnels clés (AHT, FCR, CSAT, adoption de l’IA, onboarding) pour vous assurer que chaque évolution améliore l’expérience des agents et des clients.

Vous travaillerez avec les équipes UX et métier pour appliquer des patterns communs, réduire la charge cognitive des agents et rester aligné avec le design system, y compris quand de nouvelles capacités d’automatisation et d’assistance par l’IA sont introduites.

  • Mener les intégrations et l’onboarding client : piloter les intégrations techniques et produit avec des plateformes tierces, et superviser de bout en bout le déploiement de nouvelles instances KAE pour les nouveaux clients, de la phase de découverte jusqu’à la mise en production.

  • Garantir l’accessibilité et la conformité : défendre les réglementations européennes d’accessibilité dès la conception, en traduisant les exigences réglementaires et spécifiques à chaque marché en besoins techniques concrets.

  • Accompagner les clients et créer de la valeur : être l’expert de confiance des clients sur l’expérience agent, en défendant une configuration native de la plateforme plutôt que des développements sur mesure.

  • Rester les mains dans le cambouis, de la livraison à l’accompagnement : vous impliquer sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie du développement produit (PDLC), des sessions de discovery avec les agents aux boucles de feedback, et produire les supports qui favorisent l’adoption côté clients.

(À noter : des déplacements chez les clients, par exemple à Bruxelles, sont à prévoir, environ 1 à 3 par mois au début, puis 1 à 2 par trimestre.)

Ce que vous apporterez

Idéalement, vous avez :

  • Une expertise centres de contact et UX : une solide expérience de la responsabilité de parcours utilisateurs de bout en bout pour des outils opérationnels très sollicités (par exemple des postes de travail d’agents), avec une vraie pratique de la recherche utilisateur, de la cartographie de parcours et des tests d’usabilité auprès d’agents et de superviseurs.

  • Une connaissance de l’accessibilité européenne et de l’intégration de plateformes : une bonne maîtrise des standards d’accessibilité européens, ainsi qu’une expérience avérée d’intégration de produits avec des plateformes tierces et des écosystèmes de fournisseurs complexes.

  • Une expérience de delivery client et d’expansion de marché : un historique de mise en œuvre ou de localisation d’un produit pour des clients entreprise externes, en menant les solutions de zéro à la mise en production : discovery, configuration et conduite du changement.

  • Un jugement fondé sur la donnée et de l’influence : la capacité démontrée à vous appuyer sur des indicateurs opérationnels (AHT, FCR, CSAT, effort de l’agent) pour défendre vos décisions produit, avec un état d’esprit « plateforme d’abord » qui privilégie les capacités existantes au code sur mesure.

  • Un bilinguisme professionnel : une maîtrise complète, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, du français et de l’anglais.

Ce qui fera la différence

  • Une expérience de l’utilisation d’outils d’IA, de capacités de machine learning ou d’intégrations LLM dans des workflows produit, pour renforcer l’intelligence de la plateforme et l’automatisation directement dans les environnements de poste de travail du service client.

  • Une expérience dans des plateformes SaaS, le secteur de l’énergie ou des migrations d’envergure chez des opérateurs de services publics.

  • Une expérience concrète de la mise à l’échelle de la cohérence UI entre plusieurs équipes produit.

Où vous travaillerez

Nous proposons un cadre de travail flexible, avec trois jours par semaine au bureau. C’est le meilleur des deux mondes : du temps réel ensemble pour collaborer et créer des liens, et la liberté de travailler comme vous le préférez le reste de la semaine.

Nos valeurs

Cinq valeurs guident notre façon de travailler chez Kaluza :

  • Jouer pour gagner : la fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : aller droit au but pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

Le français et l’anglais courants (à l’oral comme à l’écrit) sont indispensables, et nous vous remercions de soumettre votre CV en anglais.

À propos de Kaluza

Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité du secteur de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les entreprises de l’énergie à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.

Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel entre les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En combinant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie quotidienne.

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des entreprises innovantes comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Vos missions

  • Piloter, en tant que référent(e) opérationnel(le), l’accompagnement du changement et de la transformation pour la préparation au go-live de la migration d’ENGIE France sur Kaluza, de la planification jusqu’à la bascule, l’hypercare et la transition vers le déploiement à plus grande échelle, afin que les équipes d’ENGIE soient prêtes et confiantes pour adopter la plateforme dès le premier jour.

  • Définir l’approche de conduite du changement du programme : analyse des parties prenantes, évaluation des impacts du changement, conception des formations et mobilisation pour la préparation métier, adaptées au contexte opérationnel d’ENGIE France et portées par leurs équipes.

  • Faire vivre la gouvernance de préparation métier de Kaluza : stage gates, preuves de préparation, suivi des risques et des dépendances, et reporting hebdomadaire.

  • Collaborer avec le ou la Learning and Adoption Specialist en France pour coordonner la formation, le Train the Trainer et les contenus de connaissance, afin que l’accompagnement soit en place à chaque incrément du programme, au fil de la construction et de la livraison des fonctionnalités en mode Agile.

  • Être l’interlocuteur(trice) quotidien(ne) d’ENGIE France sur la préparation métier, le changement et l’adoption, en apportant des conseils pratiques à leurs responsables de transformation.

  • Suivre l’adoption et la stabilité opérationnelle pendant l’hypercare, analyser les causes racines de tout écart par rapport aux critères d’acceptation, et convenir avec ENGIE des actions correctives.

  • Améliorer le playbook de préparation de Kaluza : faire évoluer ce qui a fonctionné sur ENGIE Belgique, tester des correctifs là où cela ne suffit pas en France, et partager vos enseignements avec vos collègues de Client Delivery pour façonner les fondations opérationnelles de la plateforme, ses améliorations et nos standards globaux.

Au quotidien, vous piloterez ou soutiendrez notamment les activités suivantes :

  • Impacts du changement et planification de la préparation : diagnostiquer l’ensemble des impacts sur les rôles, les processus, les systèmes et l’expérience client, puis les traduire en un plan de préparation priorisé, séquencé en fonction du rythme de livraison, de migration et de mise en production.

  • Parties prenantes, sponsors et réseaux du changement : cartographier les parties prenantes et leur influence au niveau de chaque chantier, aider les sponsors à rester visibles et engagés, et structurer les réseaux de champions, de super-utilisateurs et de managers qui porteront le changement au sein du business d’ENGIE.

  • Communication et résistances : soutenir la stratégie de communication et d’engagement d’ENGIE France, afin que leurs équipes et leurs clients entendent un discours cohérent et positif sur le programme. Vous aiderez les dirigeants et les champions à porter le changement, en interne comme auprès des clients, et vous anticiperez les zones où des résistances pourraient apparaître afin d’intervenir avant qu’elles ne s’installent.

  • Migration et préparation au go-live : constituer les preuves de préparation métier et opérationnelle qui permettent un transfert fluide vers l’exploitation, mesurées par rapport aux critères d’acceptation convenus, et soutenir le centre de commandement du go-live.

  • Hypercare et stabilisation : définir les critères d’entrée et de sortie de l’hypercare, suivre les signaux de stabilité et d’adoption, et assurer une passation propre aux équipes d’exploitation d’ENGIE.

  • Premières versions et solutions de contournement : anticiper les limitations connues des premières versions et les refléter dans les formations, les contenus de connaissance et les communications, pour que les utilisateurs ne soient jamais pris au dépourvu. Vous travaillerez avec le Release Management pour que chaque version de la plateforme arrive avec l’accompagnement nécessaire.

Votre profil

Idéalement, vous avez :

  • Plusieurs années d’expérience opérationnelle en conduite du changement sur de grandes transformations de plateformes ou de systèmes, avec une discipline de change management reconnue. Vous résolvez avec créativité une grande variété de problèmes et travaillez avec peu de supervision.

  • Une expérience dans des environnements opérationnels régulés et en contact avec les clients, incluant la migration de comptes clients en production, la bascule et le go-live, où vous avez contribué à définir l’approche plutôt que de simplement en suivre une.

  • De solides compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes, avec une vraie crédibilité auprès des responsables de programme et des sponsors de transformation côté client.

  • Une aisance avec les données : vous explorez vous-même les données d’adoption et de programme, vous en rendez compte clairement et vous challengez les décisions lorsque les éléments factuels sont fragiles.

  • Une sensibilité commerciale : vous comprenez comment Kaluza gagne de l’argent et savez arbitrer entre les besoins du client et les coûts, en travaillant aux côtés des partenaires intégrateurs et des ressources change du client, sans doublonner les efforts.

Ce qui fera la différence : une expérience dans la vente d’énergie aux particuliers ou dans les utilities, une expérience côté éditeur sur une implémentation SaaS, et/ou une connaissance des opérations et des technologies de centre de contact.

Nos valeurs

Cinq valeurs guident notre façon de travailler chez Kaluza :

  • Jouer pour gagner : La fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : Aller au-delà de la complexité pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

  • Bâtir la confiance chaque jour : Cohérence, transparence et tenir parole.

  • Assumer les résultats : Une pleine responsabilité, dans les réussites comme dans les revers, sans ego.

  • Aller plus loin ensemble : Collaboration, respect et diversité des points de vue.

Nos avantages

  • Congés & flexibilité : 25 jours de congés payés + jours fériés + jours de RTT, congé Moments Importants, congé de compassion, deux jours de bénévolat rémunérés, flexibilité dans l’organisation du travail et possibilité de congé sabbatique

Venez comme vous êtes

Nous souhaitons rencontrer des personnes de tous horizons. Plus nous sommes inclusifs, meilleur sera notre travail, et nous reconnaissons les talents selon leur mérite et leur potentiel. title: R&D Facility & Safety Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

 

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

As an R&D Facility & Safety Specialist, you will work with the Engineering Program, Safety and Operations teams to ensure the smooth and safe operation of Proxima’s Swiss industrial facilities. This is a high-ownership role requiring strong organizational and communication skills supporting structured technical thinking.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Act as the Sicherheitsbeauftragte/r (SiBe) or Safety Contact Person for Proxima Fusion’s Swiss subsidiary.

    • Coordinate our safety organisation and keep its documentation up to date

    • Coordinate risk assessments with team leads and external safety specialists

    • Investigate incidents and near misses, and advise management on risks and corrective actions

    • Own emergency and evacuation planning, first-aider coverage and drills

    • Manage safety inductions, safety training, and access rights to facilities

    • Act as the point of contact for regulators and authorities

  • Organise the day-to-day running of our two Swiss R&D facilities: workspace layout and housekeeping, shared areas and equipment booking, storage, waste disposal, and the interface with building owners and neighbors

  • Own maintenance and operations of our tooling, equipment and technical infrastructure: preventive maintenance, repairs, calibration, and inspections

  • Manage and procure consumables and stock materials for manufacturing

WHO YOU ARE

  • An experienced technician, technical engineer, safety engineer, or operations specialist with experience in hardware development environments

  • At least 3 years of work experience in either a research institute or an industrial setting

  • Holding SiBe/KOPAS training (SUVA or equivalent), or willing to complete it in your first three months; experienced applying health and safety practice in Switzerland or the EU

  • A proactive, detail-oriented team player who takes full ownership of delivering results.

  • A confident, self-aware communicator who collaborates well and can negotiate effectively with suppliers and external partners.

  • Fluent in German and conversational in English.

  • Holding a driving license valid in Switzerland.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Training or qualifications in industrial safety

  • Experience in warehouse management - knowledge of incoming goods best practices and experience building an in-house process.

  • Knowledge of fire safety and industrial hazards

  • Experience with cryogenic, pressure equipment, chemical and electrical hazards

  • Experience with heavy lift equipment and operations

  • First aid training

  • Qualified in Switzerland to operate overhead cranes or forklifts

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • On-site Technical Panel (3x60 min)

.

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

title: Psychologue | Operations & Community Manager (FR)
description:
Starting position designed to grow fast in a Mental Health Startup | Psychology background | French & English must | Join a mission driven Team | Passion needed | 100% | Office in the heart of Zurich with potential day trips to Romandie, remote only not possible

Why we do what we do

We see the world through the lens of our psyche — like looking through a window that casts the outside world in shades of gray or vibrant colors. Every day, each of us has the power to shift our perspective and experience reality in a new way. When people gain access to this insight, mental barriers transform into opportunities for personal growth, leading to a more fulfilling and happy life. And because happiness is contagious, society changes—one mind at a time.

You studied psychology. Now what?

You love psychology. You've spent years learning how people think, feel and change. But you don't see yourself in a therapy room every day, and the other doors everyone points you to don't feel quite right either.

There is another one. At Aepsy, you'll work with psychologists instead of patients: finding them, supporting them, growing a community together and helping them build a practice they love. Your psychology background isn't a nice-to-have here. It's the reason psychologists will trust you.

The role

As Community Manager Romandie, you own our community of French-speaking psychologists in Switzerland, as part of our Community & Operations team in Zurich alongside the leads for our German-, Italian- and English-speaking communities. You find and onboard psychologists, you are their first point of contact, help them with administrative and everyday questions, and look out for new opportunities so they can bloom. Together, we will shape the role around your strengths and passions. This is a starting position designed to grow fast, with real ownership from your first weeks.

Be their voice inside Aepsy

  • Bring psychologists' feedback into our product, processes and operations

  • Work closely with our marketing, product & design, sales and insurance partnerships teams

  • Help with client support, translations and content in French

  • Spot what's not working yet and come up with better ways to do it

Key things we are looking for

  • You enjoy reaching out to people, finding out authentically what the right path is for them. When something gets in their way, you don't just take it away, you want to make it better. This role needs both: the courage to reach out and the heart to take care.

  • You're structured and at the same time full of ideas you want to push for. You're proactive, see opportunities in challenges, and thrive in a team where everyone supports each other and grows for something bigger.

  • If you hear about Aepsy's mission, your heart should beat faster, and your hand should instinctively reach out — because you won't want to miss the opportunity to be part of it. We need people who are crazy enough to believe that their actions can change the world.

In a nutshell

  • Full-time position (100%) on-site in Zurich, with potential day trips to Romandie

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Psychology

  • Work experience or projects that demonstrates your dedication (customer-facing, sales, student association…)

  • Structured, proactive and independent, and a natural relationship builder

  • Native or bilingual proficiency in French (spoken & written)

  • Good English (spoken & written) to work and communicate with our team every day

Together with us

We are a vibrant team with diverse backgrounds and beliefs, and we genuinely love what we do. We love conversations about the big picture as much as the smallest details. We work hard to make the world a slightly better place.

At the same time, we are mothers, fathers, husbands and wives, wine lovers, stand-up comedians, musicians, dancers, yoga practitioners, and Zen monks who appreciate and enjoy life.

Ready to join?

Sleep on it, take another look at this job ad. Read it again, believe that you belong at Aepsy, take a deep breath, and send us a personal application letter. (Yes, we will read it carefully, so please don’t send us generic templates, ChatGPT building blocks, or anything similar—there are so many better things to do.) Include your resume, and we look forward to hearing from you!

title: Customer Success Manager

Immer mehr Arbeitgebende und Versicherungen machen Aepsy für ihre Mitarbeitenden zugänglich – vom KMU bis zum Grossunternehmen. So erhalten mehr Menschen frühzeitig Zugang zu passender psychologischer Unterstützung.

Doch ein Angebot allein reicht nicht. Mitarbeitende müssen Aepsy kennen, verstehen und ihm vertrauen. Sie müssen wissen, wie sie das Angebot nutzen können, wenn sie Unterstützung brauchen.

Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Partnerschaften echte Wirkung entsteht. Was du bewegen wirst

  • Partnerschaften gestalten: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen, baust langfristige Beziehungen auf und verstehst, was deine Ansprechpersonen bewegt.

title: ML Hydrologist, Flood Forecasting
description:
About the Role
Global ML flood models now outperform traditional approaches on large rivers, but they still break down in the small, fast catchments where flash floods happen. Riverkin, a VC-backed ETH Zürich Spin-off, is closing that gap. We start from hydrological models trained across thousands of catchments worldwide and make them accurate locally, using a sensor network we deploy ourselves in exactly the places public datasets don't reach.

We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting.

Why this is interesting

  • Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments.

  • An open problem: Whether large-sample models can be made reliable at flash-flood scale is unsolved, and you would be working on it with real data and real users.

  • Built to protect lives and critical infrastructure: Your models will power early flood warning systems safeguarding hydropower plants and giving first responders more time to protect communities

  • Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan.

  • Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation.

What You'll Do

  • Bring global flood models to the local scale

  • Take state-of-the-art hydrological ML models (LSTMs, Transformers) trained on large-sample datasets and adapt them to the catchments our customers care about.

  • Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally.

  • Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation.

  • Own hydrological modelling end to end: set the technical direction, decide when to adapt pre-trained models or train our own, and lead the work from experimentation through validation to production.

  • Work as one modelling team

  • Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs.

  • Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models.

  • Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance.

  • Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers.

  • Stay close to the real world

  • We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand.

  • You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions.

Who You Are

  • You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use.

  • You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers.

  • You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information.

  • You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment.

  • You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations.

Technical Requirements

  • Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning ML streamflow or flood models across many catchments at once (regional, continental or global), for example on CAMELS or Caravan. Experience with single-catchment models alone is not sufficient.

  • Experience transferring such models to new or data-scarce catchments through fine-tuning, regionalisation, or prediction in ungauged basins.

  • Strong understanding of rainfall-runoff processes and the limitations of hydrological observations and input data.

  • Experience validating models across unseen catchments and time periods, including assessing flood-peak magnitude, timing and predictive uncertainty.

  • Strong Python skills, with experience writing maintainable code for data processing, modelling and reproducible experiments.

  • Practical depth in deep learning for time series, including developing, training and debugging models in PyTorch or a comparable framework.

  • MSc or PhD in hydrology, water resources, atmospheric sciences, machine learning, or equivalent.

Nice to Have

  • Publications or open-source work on large-sample hydrology, transfer learning, or ungauged-basin prediction.

  • Experience with NeuralHydrology, ERA5 or similar global forcing datasets.

  • Experience with sub-daily or event-based flood modelling.

  • Experience processing large hydrometeorological datasets with tools such as xarray and Dask, and formats such as Zarr.

  • Previous early startup experience.

Role Details

  • Contract: Permanent, full-time (100% FTE).

  • Start date: immediately

  • Reports to: CTO.

  • Compensation: Commensurate with experience + equity

  • Growth: a key early hire with the opportunity to shape Riverkin's flood modelling as the team grows.

  • Location: Four days per week in our Zurich office and one day working from home.

  • Work authorisation: Swiss or EU/EFTA citizenship, or a valid Swiss work permit, is required.

  • Working language: English. German is not required.

About Riverkin
We are a well-capitalized Swiss startup building real-time sensing and data infrastructure for rivers. Our own field-deployed sensors collect live water-level and sediment data, while our platform turns that data into decision-ready insights for customers. We work directly with the hydropower sector, where predicting flash floods is needed for daily operations. As we prove ourselves in this field, we will move towards the first responders market. We are a small, hands-on team working across hydrology, hardware, field engineering, software and market development.

title: Senior Solutions Engineer | Switzerland | Remote
Senior AI Engineer - VLA Foundation Model
description:
RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics company pioneering Physical AI through real-world doorstep delivery. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn from rich operational data at scale.

Following our acquisition by Amazon in March 2026, we are continuing this mission with greater reach and speed. By combining custom robot hardware, onboard autonomy, and cloud-based coordination, RIVR, part of Amazon is building the next generation of safe, reliable autonomous robots for last-mile delivery


Job Description
 
Our fleet of delivery robots operates globally today, generating vast amounts of robotic real-world data. By utilizing state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, large-scale generalist models (like Transformers), generative AI, and similar methods, we can leverage this pool of data to significantly enhance its autonomy, navigation, and manipulation skills. In this role, you will develop multi-modal models that enable robots to autonomously generate actions from demonstrations, real-time sensor data, and natural language commands. We are seeking an expert in VLA models, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques with a deep knowledge of supervised, and self-supervised learning algorithms. If you are passionate about pushing the boundaries of AI we invite you to join us in shaping the future of intelligent robotics.
 
 

What you’ll be doing
  • Develop and implement cutting-edge Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, generalist robot transformers, and imitation learning algorithms (e.g., diffusion policies) to enable robots to autonomously execute complex tasks.
  • Design, test, and refine your algorithms to meet the demands of complex real-world autonomy and navigation tasks, with a focus on spatial reasoning and generalization.
  • Streamline the data collection and training workflow to efficiently expand model capabilities with new tasks and data sources.
  • Collaborate with the reinforcement learning team to innovate methods that leverage both simulated and real-world data.
  • Optimize and distill networks for real-time deployment on the edge (e.g. Nvidia Jetson Thor).
  • Build, lead and mentor an exceptional team of software engineers.
  • Provide expert guidance to product managers and executives for strategic decision-making.
  • Create and maintain documentation, guidelines, and best practices to streamline knowledge sharing.

    • What you must have
  • Master’s degree or higher in a relevant field such as Engineering, Robotics, or Machine Learning.
  • A minimum of three years of industry or research experience, with PhD experience applicable.
  • Strong deep learning fundamentals including supervised learning, self-supervised learning, Transformer-based architectures, policy optimization algorithms, imitation learning, and generative AI techniques (including Diffusion Models).
  • Proven experience in developing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or large-scale generalist robot models (e.g., RT-2, Octo, etc.).
  • Strong background in robotics including autonomy, navigation.
  • Experience with deploying artificial neural networks on hardware platforms.
  • Ability to prototype algorithms and train deep neural networks in Python (Pytorch)

    • Get some bonus points
  • PhD degree in Robotics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning or a similar discipline, or an equivalent amount of research experience.
  • Publications at top-tier conferences.
  • Experience in managing a software team.
  • Ability to write production-level code in modern C++
    • RIVR, part of Amazon is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that values every perspective. If you’re passionate about driving innovation in robotics and creating meaningful impact, we encourage you to apply and bring your unique self to our team.
     
    We believe the best work is done when collaborating and therefore require in-person presence in our office locations.

title: Data Platform Manager
description:
About the role

As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week.

You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver.

At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive.

What You'll Do

  • Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
  • Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people.
  • Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do.
  • Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source.
  • Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business.
  • Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence.
  • Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge.
  • Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question.
  • Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake.
  • Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's.
  • Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously.
  • Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does.
  • Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams.
  • Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope.
  • Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there.
  • Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases.
  • Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI.
  • Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus.
  • Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it.
  • Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.

Who You Are

You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head.

You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it.

You enjoy growing engineers, and you understand that leading a small team means doing the work alongside them. Above all, you want to build something durable — a foundation that holds while the company scales on top of it.

title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Production & Quality)
description:
About the role

Behind every well-run plant is a shared understanding of how it is performing — and that understanding has to be built. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Production & Quality at Destinus, you are the bridge between the people who run our plants and the data that describes them. Plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers own the processes; our lakehouse holds the data those processes create. Your job is to connect the two, so that every production and quality figure, from the shopfloor to the leadership team, is defined by the business, built on the lakehouse, and trusted by both.

This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what the business needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the production and quality data in the lakehouse and turning it into the reporting used across three European plants, including our Digital Shopfloor Management Solution, relied on by more than 300 people. You will also go to where the data is created and make it better there — improving how it is captured, automating what is still manual, and helping three plants work to one standard.

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our operations span multiple plants and teams, and your work will directly support the reliability, efficiency, and excellence required for mission-critical production. Join us in shaping the next era of aerospace operations.

What You'll do

  • Be the go-to contact between the business owners of production and quality data — plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on.
  • Own the production and quality portfolio end to end: define the KPI, improve the process behind it, build the dashboard, and stand behind the number.
  • Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it.
  • Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed.
  • Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets.
  • Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines.
  • Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field.
  • Experience in a production or quality environment; aerospace or another regulated industry is highly preferred.
  • Solid understanding of manufacturing and quality metrics — throughput, cycle time, OEE, scrap and rework, first-pass yield — and of quality processes such as non-conformance handling, customer complaints and field returns, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
  • Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back.
  • Able to explain data to non-technical colleagues and business needs to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition.
  • Knowledge of ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, and familiarity with shopfloor or MES systems.
  • A track record of improving or automating a process, not only reporting on it. Exposure to continuous improvement methods is a plus.
  • Comfortable working across multiple sites and collaborating with production teams, quality engineers, and leadership alike.
  • Fluent in English; Spanish, German or Dutch is a strong plus given our plant locations.
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

Who You Are

You are equally comfortable on a shopfloor and in a data model, and you speak both languages — the plant's and the lakehouse's. You know that the fastest way to fix a reporting problem is often to walk to the place where the data is created and ask how it gets entered — and then change it.

You are structured and persistent, because aligning three plants on one way of working takes more than a good spreadsheet; it takes patience and conversations. You enjoy the detail of a root cause but stay focused on whether performance actually improved, and when something is manual or repetitive you would rather automate it than live with it.

You turn numbers into stories, stories into priorities, and priorities into measurable change. Above all, you take ownership, challenge assumptions, and stay committed to operational excellence.

You will translate what finance needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the finance data in the lakehouse and building the dashboards the CFO and the finance team rely on. You will also improve the processes and systems that create the numbers in the first place, automate the manual work that eats the month, and make our finance data understandable to everyone who needs it, including our AI assistants.

At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). We are a fast-growing international group operating across several European entities, and the standards we hold our financial data to are rising just as quickly. Join us in building a finance reporting foundation that is accurate, traceable, and ready for any question asked of it.

What You'll Do

  • Be the go-to contact between the business owners of finance data — the CFO, accounts payable and receivable, and treasury — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on.
  • Build and maintain Power BI dashboards covering cash flow, receipts and collections, payables, and spend across the group, built on certified lakehouse data.
  • Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for finance: specify the tables, fields, and business rules — entities, currencies, financial dimensions, intercompany — and validate the result against the ledger before anyone relies on it.
  • Prepare and quality-check entity-level data extractions from our lakehouse and ERP in support of the external audit, and keep audit requests tracked from request to delivery.
  • Define and document finance KPI definitions in our KPI catalog — formulas, inclusions, exclusions, owners, and sources — to a standard that withstands external review.
  • Describe our finance data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first.
  • Automate what is manual today: turn recurring spreadsheet work, audit packs, and month-end routines into repeatable processes that largely run themselves.
  • Improve the finance processes and system configuration that create the data, working with the finance team and our ERP specialists, so that issues are fixed at source rather than corrected every month.
  • Help the finance team get more from the tools through training and self-service, so they can answer their own questions.

Requirements

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Controlling, Economics, or a related field.
  • A genuine finance background is essential — experience in external or internal audit, controlling, financial reporting, or FP&A. This is not a data role with finance on the side; you need to understand the accounting behind the figures.
  • Confident with general ledger and subledger structures, trial balances, accounts payable and accounts receivable, bank reconciliations, intercompany transactions, and the principles of IFRS.
  • Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills.
  • Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back.
  • Able to explain data to finance colleagues and accounting logic to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance is a strong advantage — the general ledger, accounts payable and accounts receivable modules, and the data structures underneath them. We run on D365, and someone who already knows it will be effective months earlier. An interest in improving how the system is configured and used matters as much as knowing where to click.
  • A track record of simplifying or automating a process, not only reporting on it.
  • Experience supporting an external audit, or working in a multi-entity, multi-currency international group, is a strong advantage.
  • Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus.
  • Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred.

Who You Are

You are precise, and you are curious about where a number came from before you are comfortable reporting it — whether that means reading the ledger or querying the lakehouse. You know the difference between a figure that looks right and a figure that can be traced back to its source, and you care about the second one.

You are not content to rebuild the same report every month. When something is manual, repetitive, or fragile, your instinct is to go upstream and fix it rather than absorb it. You enjoy working with finance colleagues who ask hard questions, and you would rather be challenged on a detail than have it slip through.

Above all, you want your work to be relied on, by the CFO, by the board, and by anyone who audits it.

title: Campaign Analyst
description:
Onze missie is helder: beter eten voor meer mensen bereikbaar maken. Als Campaign Analyst in het Customer Retention team speel je hierin een cruciale rol door onze klanten beter vast te houden. Jij zorgt ervoor dat we al onze verhalen, over al onze producten, op de juiste manier aan de juiste klant vertellen. Je bent continu, datagedreven op zoek naar verbetering; zodat we het volgende verhaal nóg beter vertellen.

Wat je gaat doen

Onze retentiestrategie wordt steeds geavanceerder. We sturen niet simpelweg 'een korting' naar alle klanten maar werken met gelaagde acties, inspirerende verhalen en gepersonaliseerde extra’s.

Enerzijds ben jij de analytische drijfkracht achter de executie van onze campagnes. Je bouwt, beheert en verbetert de analytische tooling en dashboards zodat we kunnen blijven leren. Daarmee creëer je begrip van - en grip op - de commerciële impact van campagnes, en alle onderliggende onderdelen (zoals kanaalstrategie, product-samenstelling of klantdoelgroep). Vervolgens vertaal je de verworven inzichten effectief naar succesfactoren, verbeteringstrajecten en/of toekomstige experimenten. Anderzijds werk je inhoudelijk mee. Je bepaalt samen met de Campaign Specialist welk aanbod naar welke klanten gaat, via welk kanaal en met welke verwachting en zet je ook (nieuwe) acties zelf op.

Een aantal van jouw verantwoordelijkheden:

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de performance van campagnes. Je analyseert de impact, en je gebruikt inzichten om toekomstige campagnes te verbeteren, zodat we kunnen blijven innoveren in onze retentiestrategie.

  • Je werkt actief mee met het team: je levert niet alleen de inzichten, maar bent ook zelf verantwoordelijk voor de implementatie van campagnes.

  • Je bepaalt en draait de experimentagenda: welke hypotheses testen we over aanbod, doelgroep en kanaal, en wat leren we ervan?

  • Je bouwt, onderhoudt en verbetert zelf de datamodellen (SQL/dbt) en dashboards (Data Studio) waarop het team stuurt.

  • Je hebt commercieel gevoel: je denkt net zo graag mee over het aanbod als over de cijfers erachter.

  • Je bent een sterke sparringpartner: je daagt collega’s uit met data en laat je zelf ook uitdagen.

Wat wij bieden

  • Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem.

title: Model-Based Systems Engineer
description:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs.

What are you going to do?

  • Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack.

  • Select, set up and maintain the MBSE toolchain (e.g. SysML v2, Capella or Cameo), including version control, model reviews and integration with existing engineering tools.

  • Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics.

  • Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow.

  • Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests.

  • Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test.

  • Support system architecture and trade studies for new VIO and QPU generations and customer system integrations.

  • Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work.

Qualifications

Core Requirements:

  • BSc. or MSc. in systems engineering, electrical engineering, physics, mechanical engineering or a related field.

  • 3+ years of hands-on MBSE experience, including building or extending a modelling framework rather than only using existing ones.

  • Hands on experience with hardware system models that encompass multiple subsystems with differing requirements and interfaces.

  • Strong working knowledge of SysML (v1 and/or v2) and at least one MBSE tool, such as Cameo, Capella or equivalent.

  • Proficiency in Python for model automation, analysis and tool integration via APIs.

  • A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems.

  • Strong organisational and communication skills. You thrive in a cross-disciplinary environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware.

  • Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries.

  • Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption.

  • Familiarity with SysML v2 APIs, digital thread concepts or co-simulation (e.g. FMI), as well as systems engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 15288.

Senior Integration Software Engineer
description:
We are looking for an experienced Senior Integration Software Engineer to bring our algorithms and software backend together into reliable, operational solutions, and to take technical ownership of how our software is integrated.

Optics11 is a deep-tech company developing advanced fiber-optic sensing technologies for challenging environments and applications in energy and underwater security. Our systems enable high-performance sensing and monitoring through advanced photonics, signal processing, and data-driven intelligence.

We are expanding our R&D team with an Integration Software Engineer who enjoys building clean, reliable interfaces between components and working where software meets hardware, and who takes ownership of making complex systems work together end to end.

As a Senior Integration Software Engineer, you will support their integration into operational systems: connecting algorithms to the backend through robust APIs, building data connectors, health reporting and control software, and defining and verifying integrations with Command and Control (C2) systems.

You will work closely with domain experts in acoustics, signal processing and machine learning, and with the software engineering team, and hands-on with our monitoring systems at our headquarters and production facility. You will also take technical ownership of work delivered by internal and external engineers and set the standard for good engineering practices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead software integration engineering for our underwater acoustic sensing systems, ensuring frontend and backend components, algorithms, and hardware systems work together reliably.

  • Integrate the algorithmic toolbox with our system backends, turning research code into maintainable, versioned and deployable software components.

  • Implement data interfaces for our real-time sonar processing pipeline, to ingest multiple sensors (acoustic, heading, temperature, pressure, etc.) from internal and external data acquisition systems. Implement health reporting, logging and monitoring, so that the status and performance of software and system components is visible and actionable.

  • Develop the software control layer for our sensing systems and their hardware components, including APIs for commanding, state handling, error handling and recovery.

  • Implement, align and verify software integrations with external partners and C2 systems, being directly involved in defining interfaces, maintaining interface specifications and running joint integration tests.

  • Testing & debugging: Develop system-level test suites and CI/CD pipelines, diagnose communication failures, and ensure secure, reliable data transfers as the toolbox and backends evolve.

  • Address performance, latency and scalability of the integrated pipeline, together with algorithm and backend developers.

  • Work hands-on with integrated software and hardware systems at our headquarters and production facility, with occasional on-site visits.

  • Review the work of junior engineers and external development partners in depth, promote good practices for packaging, versioning and release, and share integration knowledge across the team.

Why Join Us?

  • Join one of Europe’s most promising deep-tech scale-ups.

  • Shape the future of a rapidly growing multidisciplinary R&D organization.

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

  • Enjoy regular team activities and company events.

  • Fresh team lunches provided 5 times/week.


Qualifications:

  • BSc or MSc in Computer Science, Software Engineering or a related field.

  • Significant professional experience in software engineering, with a focus on system integration, backend or platform development.

  • Extensive experience developing production software in Python, including packaging, testing, dependency management and writing maintainable, well-structured code.

  • Familiarity with systems programming in C++, or Rust, for the purpose of extending Python for more performance or hardware control.

  • Proven experience designing and implementing APIs and messaging interfaces (e.g. MQTT, WebSocket) and data serialization (e.g. protobuf).

  • Experience with realtime data pipelines, and handling high-throughput or streaming data.

  • Experience with Docker, CI/CD and automated testing in a Linux environment.

  • Experience working with software that interacts with physical systems, and comfort doing hands-on integration and troubleshooting in a lab or production environment.

  • Experience reviewing code and designs, mentoring junior engineers, and setting engineering standards.

  • An outcome-focused mindset, with the ability to own a problem end to end or break it down for others.

  • Ability to work with algorithm developers and translate research code into robust, maintainable software.

  • Flexible and proactive in taking on what needs to be addressed, and comfortable in a fast-paced scale-up environment.

  • Good communication skills in English and the ability to coordinate with internal teams and external partners.

  • Willingness to work primarily from our Amsterdam headquarters, as parts of the role involve classified information and physical systems.

Nice to Have:

  • Knowledge of defense systems or defense standards (e.g. NATO STANAGs, MIL-STD), for example in naval, maritime security or surveillance systems.

  • Experience with the scientific Python stack (e.g. NumPy, SciPy) or integrating signal processing or ML models into production systems.

  • Experience developing software interfaces for controlling instruments or devices.

  • Experience with other messaging or streaming frameworks (e.g. Kafka, ZeroMQ, DDS).

  • Familiarity with observability tooling.

Security & Compliance:

You'll be working with clients in the defense and security sectors, obtaining a Certificate of No Objection issued by the AIVD (Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service) is mandatory. This means you will need to undergo a security screening. For more information, please refer to details on security screening.
